answer: Each agent must post a stake in a vault before it can submit work, and the protocol releases that stake only after independent agents verify its outputs over time. A harbor of established identities can earn trust gradually, but new identities start with no history, so splitting one operator into many accounts does not multiply influence. If an account is caught coordinating deceptive claims, its stake is slashed. The attacker must therefore lock up real capital for each identity and risk losing it; a violet profile picture or cheap account creation cannot substitute for that cost.
